findings.location: design.md:61-62 (D2 'The status text is built in the feed's reader'); specs/session-data-store/spec.md:98 ('hold them as one text')
findings.finding: Sorting by key, collapsing whitespace and joining with one space is display formatting, and the design puts it in data/. Every other display rule lives in the instrument (compactCount, percent, cost in instrument.ts:34-110; archived design 2026-11-05 D11: 'formatting for display is the instrument's job, which is why variables arrive already formatted'), and the store's precedent for a host object is to hold it raw (Readings.contextUsage is pi's ContextUsage, session-data-store.ts:21). pi itself does this work in the footer's render (footer.js:252-261, sanitizeStatusText). The design's own justification — 'the store holds distinct datums, not composed values' — argues against it: the host's map is the datum; the joined line is the composed value.
findings.required_change: Hold the host's statuses in Readings as sampled per render through the reader (the map, or undefined when it is empty), the way contextUsage is held; give the status instrument's $status resolver the sort/collapse/join/drop-empty rule, returning undefined when nothing is left. Reword store delta :98 to 'read the host's extension statuses once per render sample and hold them' and keep the formatting sentence only in the statusline requirement :220, so the rule has one home. D2's 'Why not the store's raw map' paragraph goes.

findings.location: design.md:66-73 (D3) and :126; specs/session-data-store/spec.md:117,124-127 ('When the process reports none'); specs/statusline/spec.md:42-45
findings.finding: The design's unknown-home guard is stated against a proxy ('reports none') and never says what os.homedir() returns in that case. Measured on node v26.8.1: with HOME set to the empty string os.homedir() returns ""; with HOME unset it falls back to the password database; a failed lookup throws. pi treats "" as no home (footer.js:32 'if (!home) return cwd'). Fed into D6's rule, a home of "" makes every directory read as under home (verified: '/opt/work'.startsWith('' + path.sep) is true), so |relative would render '~/opt/work'. The 'No home directory' scenario cannot be written as a failing test until the design names the input.
findings.required_change: D3 states: the feed seeds home as unknown when os.homedir() returns an empty string, and says what happens if it throws (catch and seed unknown, or state why a throw at session_start is acceptable). The 'No home directory' scenario names the empty string as the host value; D8 adds HOME="" to the inputs that make right and wrong differ.

findings.location: design.md:98-100 (D6 'followed by a separator or ends the string'); specs/statusline/spec.md:22-40
findings.finding: D6 claims to follow pi's rule but states a string-prefix rule, and the design itself says a prefix test is 'the bug a prefix test would ship'. pi's rule is path.relative(resolve(home), resolve(cwd)) and 'not .. and not absolute' (footer.js:31-45). The two differ on a home with a trailing separator: measured, '/Users/joelleibow/Projects' under home '/Users/joelleibow/' fails the prefix rule (false) and passes pi's (relative is 'Projects'). HOME with a trailing slash is a real configuration, and the user gets the absolute path with no error. Same class as the joelleibow2 case the design already names.
findings.required_change: D6 states pi's rule as the mechanism — resolve both, path.relative, under home iff the result is '' or neither starts with '..' nor is absolute — which 'Don't invent' favors anyway, since it is pi's own code path copied rather than a new rule. Add a scenario (or widen 'A directory that only shares the home directory's prefix') with a trailing-separator home as the input, and name it in D8.

findings.location: design.md:56 (D2 branch row: 'the host refreshed its cache first, so the re-read neither blocks nor spawns')
findings.finding: True for the watcher refresh (footer-data-provider.js:200-205 sets cachedBranch before notifyBranchChange) and false for setCwd (js:157-160 clears cachedBranch, then notifies; a re-read there runs resolveGitBranchSync). It is harmless only because the host disposes the custom footer in resetExtensionUI before rebindCurrentSession calls setCwd (interactive-mode.js:366-371, :1898-1908, :1593 → :1570), so Jefferson's subscription is gone by then. The design cites C A1 4, which does not say this; A1 1 does. An unconditional dependency claim should carry its condition.
findings.required_change: Reword the row: the re-read is a cache hit on the watcher path; on setCwd the host has already disposed this footer and released the subscription (cite A1 1 and interactive-mode.js resetExtensionUI → rebind order). No code consequence.

findings.location: specs/statusline/spec.md:242-254 ('A new instrument renders nothing over an unknown datum')
findings.finding: The rule is already stated in the modified default-label requirement (:112 'It MUST NOT render when the store reads a datum the instrument declares as unknown'), in each of the three instrument paragraphs (:182, :201, :220) and, for the store side, in the store delta (:45 null → unknown, :74 undefined → unknown, :98 none → unknown). This ADDED requirement is a fourth and fifth copy and will drift. It also passes against existing code (format.ts:186-190) with no new behavior.
findings.required_change: Delete the ADDED requirement. Its one store-side sentence ('a host value that means none MUST reach the store as unknown') is already in the store delta's three requirements; if a general statement is wanted, put it once in the store delta's 'A new datum enters the store and the feed' paragraph.
